brief: JPM's Nov 2 Afternoon Briefing reads October's ISM manufacturing survey as a Goldilocks print: the production index hit a four-year high at 59.0 and employment stayed firm even as price pressures remained elevated, so JPM says Tech looks oversold but not yet all-clear, keeping the broadening trade into Cyclicals, SMid-Caps, Financials and Consumer as where money should go. Desk color shows GOOGL and AMZN bouncing on bond-market financing access while financing-constrained Neoclouds CRWV and NBIS keep selling off; SMH reclaims its 200-day average even as CPU-linked shorts persist post-INTC, and CHKP and OKTA stay under pressure. On the midterms, JPM assigns 66% to a Blue Wave, 26% to a split Dem House/GOP Senate Congress and 7% to a Red Wave, each with a modest SPX move, and cites SPX seasonality with a 100% hit rate 6-12 months after midterms since 1990. Separately, JPM reiterates its Tactically Bullish call: strong household balance sheets and record corporate margins argue against recession risk, leaving Middle East re-escalation, already priced into oil, as the main non-AI downside risk.
